reigns.note: Eponymous lord of Phylace whose halls held Melampus and whose cattle were guarded there — grandfather of the Phthian captains Protesilaus and Podarces. Distinct from the Phylacus slain in Iliad 6 and from the Delphic local hero.
Son of Phylacus, rich in flocks, left behind in Phylace when the Argo sailed — father of Protesilaus and Podarces. Distinct from Iphiclus son of Thestius.
Warlike leader of those who held Phylace and the Phthian towns; first Achaean ashore at Troy, slain before his house in Phylace was fully established.
Younger brother of Protesilaus who marshalled the Phthians when the host longed for their fallen leader — successor of the Phylace contingent at Troy.
